text:
emma: hey team, second day. copied dotfiles from the repo and followed the quickstart. shell shows node 18 via asdf, but GUI apps (slack's dev tools / mac app) open a shell with old brew node. getting mismatch errors when running local scripts. what am i missing?

oliver: welcome! :wave: macOS launches different shells for GUI vs terminal. put PATH + asdf init in ~/.zprofile (login shells) and not in .zshrc only. GUI apps opened from Finder/Spotlight won't get your interactive RC by default. you can launch apps from terminal (open -a) to inherit envs.

emma: ah makes sense. i had everything in .zshrc. quick snippet anyone uses?

shay: minimal we use in ~/.zprofile: 

  export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"
  if command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/bin:$PATH"
  fi
  . "$(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh"  # asdf init

keep .zshrc for completions and fast stuff.

emma: thanks. another thing: npm global installs try to write to /usr/local and npm suggests using sudo. i'd rather not. recommended fix?

oliver: create ~/.npmrc with `prefix=${HOME}/.npm-global` and add `export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"` to your profile. or just use asdf node so global installs are inside the node runtime managed by asdf. avoid sudo.

emma: node-gyp native builds are failing because of OpenSSL headers too. brew has openssl@3 in /opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3. what envs do you set?

shay: for native builds set CPPFLAGS/LDFLAGS to brew's paths before installing native modules: 

  export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"
  export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"

then `npm rebuild` or reinstall the package.

emma: random dotfiles question: the link script tries to overwrite existing configs and i lost some local changes. how do you usually manage dotfiles safely?

oliver: we recommend backing up before linking. simple pattern in our repo: `mv ~/.bashrc ~/.bashrc.pre-onboard 2>/dev/null || true` then symlink. some folks use GNU stow to manage groups. open a PR if you want the script to prompt/backup.

emma: awesome. last thing: VSCode integrated terminal doesn't load the env vars from .env.local for my React app tests. terminal in iTerm sees them. any VSCode config?

shay: VSCode may start shells non-login. set `terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx` to `['-l']` for zsh to force login, or in your launch.json use "envFile": "${workspaceFolder}/.env.local". direnv is also handy for per-project envs; we have a sample .envrc in the dotfiles repo.

emma: perfect. followed these, fixed the PATH order, reshimmed asdf, and now everything lines up. thanks all :raised_hands:

dev-setup-bot: Welcome @emma! Helpful links: dotfiles repo https://git.internal/redwood/dotfiles, onboarding checklist https://internal.redwood.dev/onboard, add ssh key to gitlab and join #dev-setup. If you need elevated access for asdf plugins, ping @infra.

emma: will do, i'll also add my editor + common tweaks to the onboarding doc.
